channel.description: Latest articles from Business Today India (businesstoday.in)

item.title: BSE shares hit new high: Analysts raise price targets after solid Q3; STT may dent volumes
item.description: Brokerage firms continue to remain positive on BSE Ltd after the exchange reported a strong quarterly performance in the December 2025 quarter.

item.title: White House revises fact sheet on India-US trade deal: No mention of ‘pulses’, ‘intends’ instead of ‘commits’ for $500 bn imports
item.description: India-US trade deal: White House has revised the fact sheet on the deal, removing pulses and changing the language of the terms.

item.title: Elon Musk’s xAI sees co-founder exit, Jimmy Ba bids farewell
item.description: Two xAI co-founders step down within hours, raising questions about internal shifts following its SpaceX merger.

item.title: Delhi Police issues notice to Penguin Random House over Gen Naravane’s unpublished memoir
item.description: Gen Naravane book controversy: The notice has instructed Penguin to join the inquiry and clarify the circumstances under which the manuscript became available before its formal launch.

item.title: Varun Beverages shares extend 2025 losing streak; time to sell?
item.description: Varun Beverages share price: Analysts have attributed competitive pressure from Reliance-owned Coca Cola, the potential initial public offering (IPO) of Coca-Cola Beverages India business and high operating costs behind weakness in the stock.

item.title: Cyient, TCS, Infosys could be IT contra bets: SMIFS' Sharad Avasthi; shares views on jewellery, mid- & small-caps
item.description: "IT could be a contra bet and that's one space where we are thinking because of the uncertainty around AI. Some IT stocks have become attractive," Sharad Avasthi told Business Today.

item.title: Geopolitics of GPUs: How the US-India interim deal shields New Delhi’s AI ambitions
item.description: The latest interim agreement on reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade between the US and India now offers what industry observers describe as strategic reassurance. It does not change export rules overnight. But it signals alignment.

item.title: Hope India-US deal doesn’t mean India-Russia ties suffer: Russian minister Sergei Ryabkov
item.description: “Tariffs and coercive measures of all sorts are unacceptable ways to establish one-power dominance,” said Sergei Ryabkov in an interview.
